reason: E1 directly supports premises 1-3 by reporting ~110% elongation in CoCrFeNi nanopillars and attributing it to SFE variations from atomic heterogeneities driving twinning-dislocation synergy. E3 supports premise 4 by showing twinning-controlled deformation enhances strength and ductility in CrCoNi, with DFT indicating negative SFE and high twinning propensity. Premise 5 (intentional enhancement of heterogeneity) is not directly supported by the cited evidence; E2 discusses precipitates in a BCC alloy, which is unrelated to the proposed FCC HEA mechanism.
premises: Atomic-level compositional heterogeneities in FCC HEAs cause wide variations in generalized stacking fault energy (SFE).
SFE variations promote spatial coordination of deformation twinning and dislocation slip.
This synergistic twinning-dislocation activity leads to ultrahigh uniform tensile ductility (e.g., ~110%) at high flow stress in nanopillars.
Deformation nano-twinning is a prominent deformation mode in FCC HEAs/MEAs that enhances strength and ductility.
Local SFE variations can be intentionally enhanced by micro-alloying or compositional gradients.
